solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Suspect clues introduced by agent matter fundamentally (9)

indicatorNotes.Suspect: suspect, as an adjective, means dodgy or not to be trusted, so the letters are not in their proper order
indicatorNotes.introduced by: the anagrammed word is brought in after the agent, so the agent comes first

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
CLUES rearranged

annotation.surface: A detective is handed dubious clues by a secret agent, and the whole business matters deeply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect clues' looks like a detective's worry; 'suspect' is the anagram instruction and 'agent' is the standard crossword MOLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Molecules are the basic units that matter is made of, so they are matter at its most fundamental.

entries.clue: Smuggler penning final letter in duplicate — it’s at gunpoint (6)

indicatorNotes.penning: to pen is to enclose, so the smuggler holds the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.final letter: the final letter of the alphabet, Z
indicatorNotes.in duplicate: in duplicate means two copies, so Z twice

blocks.note: a mule carries contraband across a border
Z, the last letter, written twice; it goes between MU and LE

annotation.surface: A smuggler writes out a letter twice while someone holds a gun on him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Final letter' reads like the last letter the smuggler writes; it is the last letter of the alphabet. The definition is playful: the muzzle is literally the point of a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: The muzzle is the open end of a gun barrel, the very point the shot leaves from.

entries.clue: Trap leaderless gangster parking in building site (7,3)

indicatorNotes.leaderless: without a leader, so the first letter goes
indicatorNotes.in: the gangster and the parking go inside the building site

blocks.note: a lot is a plot of land to build on; it wraps round the rest as L…OT
MOBSTER without its M
P is the parking sign

annotation.surface: A gangster with no boss is caught parking on a building site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trap' could be a verb in the surface, but as the definition it is a noun: the basket fishermen use to catch lobsters.
annotation.definitionFit: A lobster pot is a cage-like trap lowered to the seabed to catch lobsters.

entries.clue: Cautious drawing in lad’s daily (8)

indicatorNotes.drawing in: to draw in is to pull inside, so CHARY takes LAD into itself

blocks.note: chary = wary, cautious; it wraps round LAD as CHAR…Y
straight from the clue

annotation.surface: A careful boy is sketching in his daily newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; in British English a daily is also a cleaner who comes in each day, which is what a charlady is.
annotation.definitionFit: A daily is a British term for a cleaning woman who comes every day, the same job as a charlady.

entries.clue: Look to rope in quadruped with this? (5)

annotation.definition: Look to rope in quadruped with this?

indicatorNotes.to rope in: to rope in is to capture and hold, so LO holds ASS inside it

blocks.note: lo! = look!; it wraps round the animal as L…O
a four-legged animal, the donkey

annotation.surface: A cowboy asks whether this is the tool for catching a four-legged animal.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read plainly, it describes what a lasso is for, so wordplay and definition are the same sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A lasso is the looped rope used to rope in cattle or horses.

entries.clue: Groom’s crazy about old flame (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about means turned round, so BATS is written backwards

blocks.note: bats = mad, crazy
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

annotation.surface: A bridegroom is wildly in love with a former girlfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groom' pulls toward a wedding; here it is the man who looks after horses. LEMAN is an old word worth knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: A groom is someone who looks after horses, which is exactly what a stableman does.

entries.clue: Six day nurses run practice of excellence (6)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold closely, so the six and the day hold R between them

blocks.note: Roman numeral six
Tuesday, abbreviated
R = run, as on a cricket scoreboard; it sits between VI and TUE

annotation.surface: Nurses on a six-day rota keep up the highest standards of care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like the hospital staff; it is the verb, holding R inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Virtue is moral excellence shown in how one behaves, the habitual practice of being good.

entries.clue: Adverse criticism of lakeside houses (4)

indicatorNotes.houses: to house is to contain, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of 'of' and the start of 'lakeside'

annotation.surface: People complain about the lakeside homes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' reads as the buildings by the lake; it is the verb that holds the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Flak is heavy criticism, borrowed from the anti-aircraft fire of the same name.

entries.clue: Cut off my daughter ringing up before noon (8)

indicatorNotes.ringing: to ring is to encircle, so COR and D surround the rest
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
D = daughter; CORD wraps round the rest as COR…D
ere = before, in old or poetic English
N = noon

annotation.surface: Someone telephones their daughter before midday and has the call cut off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My daughter ringing up' paints a phone call; 'my' is the exclamation COR, and 'ringing' surrounds rather than telephones.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone with every way out blocked has been cut off from escape.

entries.clue: Catch on toilet sticks in this makeshift shelter (7)

blocks.note: to twig is to catch on, to understand
loo is British for toilet

annotation.surface: Someone snags their clothing on a lavatory built from branches.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition hints at the wordplay: a twigloo is an igloo-shaped den of twigs, so 'sticks' describe what it is built from.
annotation.definitionFit: A twigloo is a dome-shaped shelter made from sticks, the kind built in the woods for camping or play.

entries.clue: Cross evacuated zone with military officers (7)

indicatorNotes.evacuated: emptied out, so only the outside letters of ZONE remain

blocks.note: ZONE with its middle removed
the brass are the senior officers

annotation.surface: Senior officers are angry at a war zone that has been cleared of people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; here it is a noun, a hybrid animal, and a zebrass is the offspring of a zebra and a donkey.
annotation.definitionFit: A zebrass is a cross between a zebra and an ass.

entries.clue: Acceptable charges overturned after tax reminder (5)

indicatorNotes.charges: to charge is to load, so OK is loaded into the reversed word
indicatorNotes.overturned: turned over, so NET reads backwards

blocks.note: net pay is what remains after tax; reversed to TEN, it wraps round OK as T…EN
OK = acceptable

annotation.surface: Fees that are reasonable once tax is taken off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like fees, which fits 'tax'; it is the verb, loading OK into TEN.
annotation.definitionFit: A token is a keepsake that reminds you of someone or something.

entries.clue: Hooter set in oil well blasted a couple of times (6,3)

indicatorNotes.set in: the two times are placed inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.blasted: blown up, so OIL WELL is scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: OIL WELL rearranged; it opens as LI…LEOWL
T = time, twice; it sits after LI

annotation.surface: A car horn sounds twice on an oil rig that has been blown up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn or siren; a hooter is also a bird that hoots.
annotation.definitionFit: The little owl is a small European owl, and owls are hooters.

entries.clue: European aircraft holding 100 men one could expel (7)

blocks.note: E = European
a jet; it wraps round C as JE…T
C is the Roman numeral for 100
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: A European plane carries a hundred soldiers, one of whom might be thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase standing for a noun: an ejector is one that could expel.
annotation.definitionFit: An ejector is a device or person that throws something out, one that could expel.

entries.clue: Last header on target — own goal scored by United attack (5,2,3)

indicatorNotes.header on: the header, the first letter, of TARGET
indicatorNotes.scored by: the own goal is marked by United, taking U into its middle

blocks.note: first letter of target
OG = own goal, as in football reports; it wraps round U as O…G
U = United, as in football team names
to hit out is to attack

annotation.surface: A football report: a late header, then an own goal as United press forward.
annotation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'Last' look like a final header; it is the verb, to endure.
annotation.definitionFit: Last as a verb means to endure to the end, and toughing it out is enduring through hardship.

entries.clue: Single bit of evidence attorney put before Corporation (5)

indicatorNotes.put before: the attorney comes first, before the corporation

blocks.note: DA = district attorney, the US prosecutor
a corporation is an old humorous word for a large belly, a tum

annotation.surface: A lawyer presents one piece of evidence against a company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' fits the courtroom as a company in the dock; it is the old joke word for a pot belly.
annotation.definitionFit: A datum is one item of data, a single piece of information or evidence.

entries.clue: Silicon based mineral is a sort of geyserite (6-3)

indicatorNotes.a sort of: to sort is to rearrange, so GEYSERITE is put into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A mineralogist classifies a silica mineral as a variety of geyserite.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is plausible geology, since geyserite really is a silica deposit, and 'a sort of' reads as a variety rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Tiger's-eye is a golden-brown gemstone made of quartz, a silicon-based mineral.

entries.clue: Cheesy sauce over puff pastry for starters (5)

indicatorNotes.over: the sauce is spread over the letters, covering them on both sides
indicatorNotes.for starters: only the starting letters of puff and pastry

blocks.note: soy sauce; it wraps round PP as SO…Y
first letters of puff and pastry

annotation.surface: A cheese sauce poured over puff pastry as an appetiser.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all cooking, and 'Cheesy' seems to describe the sauce; it is the definition, meaning sentimental.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheesy and soppy both mean sentimental in a cloying, overdone way.

entries.clue: Criminal perhaps might pinch one (8)

indicatorNotes.Criminal: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
I = one, the Roman numeral
PERHAPS holds the I; the whole lot is then rearranged

annotation.surface: A thief might well steal one.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a sapphire is exactly what a criminal might pinch.
annotation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gemstone, the kind of thing a thief might steal.

entries.clue: Head of Scotland Yard team (5)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Scotland
a quad, or quadrangle, is an enclosed yard

annotation.surface: The chief of the London police heads a unit of detectives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scotland Yard' reads as the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London; the two words are split, one giving S and the other QUAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A squad is a small team, of players or police officers.

entries.clue: Sister keeping concept manuscript pieces close at hand (8)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the sister keeps the concept inside her abbreviation

blocks.note: SR = Sister, the title abbreviation; it wraps round IDEA as S…R
idea = concept
MS = manuscript

annotation.surface: A nun holds on to her draft pages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' is slang for guns, and sidearms are the ones worn on the belt, close at hand.
annotation.definitionFit: Sidearms are pistols worn at the side, weapons kept close at hand.

entries.clue: Spirits guiding information I repeated (5)

indicatorNotes.repeated: said twice, so I becomes II

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
I written twice

annotation.surface: Guardian spirits pass on knowledge again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: Genii is a plural of genie, and also of genius in its old sense of a guardian spirit.
annotation.definitionFit: Genii are spirits, whether genies or guardian spirits of a place or person.

entries.clue: Servant carrying too much soup (7)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the servant carries the other letters inside

blocks.note: a page is a young servant; it wraps round OTT as P…AGE
OTT = over the top

annotation.surface: A waiter is carrying far too much soup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too much' seems to describe the amount of soup; it is OTT, over the top.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain, rather old-fashioned synonym for a thick vegetable soup, as in Esau's mess of pottage.

entries.clue: National song book collection purloined by attention seeker (6)

indicatorNotes.purloined by: stolen by, so the thief takes the books into itself

blocks.note: ahem is the cough used to get attention; it wraps round NT as A…HEM
NT = New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

annotation.surface: Someone who wants to be noticed steals a book of national songs.
annotation.walkthrough: The attention seeker is not a person but the sound 'ahem'.
annotation.definitionFit: Every country has an official song sung on state occasions; the national anthem is it.

entries.clue: Lout failing to start puzzle (6)

indicatorNotes.failing to start: the word does not get its start, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: FLUMMOX without its F

annotation.surface: A thug can't even begin to solve a puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' is the verb flummox, to baffle, not the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A lummox is a clumsy, stupid oaf, a lout.

entries.clue: Cardinal is essentially parish priest in red uniform (9)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence, the central letters, of PARISH
indicatorNotes.in: the priest goes inside the red

blocks.note: the middle two letters of paRIsh
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, a red; it wraps round ELI as CH…E
Eli is the priest in the Bible's book of Samuel
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A cardinal is really just a parish priest dressed up in red robes.
annotation.walkthrough: Cardinals do wear red, which makes the surface convincing; 'red' is Che Guevara, the communist revolutionary.
annotation.definitionFit: Cardinal Richelieu was the powerful chief minister of Louis XIII of France.

entries.clue: Her sweet drops could be like sugar-lumps (5)

indicatorNotes.drops: to drop is to let go, so HER falls out

blocks.note: the letters to remove
CHERUBIC, sweet as a cherub, without HER

annotation.surface: A woman's sweets, spilled on the floor, look like sugar cubes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet drops' looks like boiled sweets; 'sweet' is cherubic and 'drops' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Sugar lumps are small cubes, so they could be described as cubic.

entries.clue: Clobber worn by a bishop? (5)

indicatorNotes.worn by: HIT goes around A and B, like clothes worn by a body

blocks.note: to clobber is to hit; it wraps round AB as H…IT
straight from the clue
B = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: What clothes might a bishop wear?
annotation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes, so the whole clue also defines a habit, the robe of a monk or nun; the question mark flags that a bishop is only a loose example.
annotation.definitionFit: A habit is the long robe worn by members of a religious order.

entries.clue: American’s ready for stag, perhaps (4)

blocks.note: ready, or readies, is British slang for cash, so this asks for American slang for a dollar
the male of several kinds of deer, a stag being one example

annotation.surface: An American is prepared for a stag night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not prepared but British slang for money, as in readies, so an American's ready is a buck.
annotation.definitionFit: A buck is an American dollar, and a buck is also a male deer such as a stag.

entries.clue: Bush sheltering a river location where drinkers gather (7)

indicatorNotes.sheltering: the bush shelters the other letters inside it

blocks.note: broom is a yellow-flowered shrub; it wraps round AR as B…ROOM
straight from the clue
R = river

annotation.surface: A bush by the riverbank where people gather to drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bush' is the shrub broom, not the sweeping brush.
annotation.definitionFit: A barroom is the room of a pub or inn where drinks are served.

entries.clue: County Kerry condemned hard border (7)

indicatorNotes.condemned: something condemned is wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up

blocks.note: CO = county
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An Irish county condemns a hard border with Northern Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: County Kerry is a real Irish county, and 'hard border' calls up Brexit; it is a garden bed made of stones.
annotation.definitionFit: A rockery is a garden border built of rocks, so it is literally hard.

entries.clue: IT execs affected by cut in US surcharge (6,3)

indicatorNotes.affected by: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged, and the cut follows them

blocks.note: IT EXECS rearranged
ax is the American spelling of axe, to cut

annotation.surface: Technology executives suffer from an American budget cut.
annotation.walkthrough: Excise is a tax on goods produced at home, such as alcohol or tobacco, added on top of the price.
annotation.definitionFit: An excise tax is a levy added to the price of particular goods, a surcharge.
